transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jon Reyes (Redwood SE), Lucas Chen (VectorGrid CTO), Amira Singh (VectorGrid Head of Infra), Tom Ruiz (VectorGrid Partnerships)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone thanks for making time, quick intros from our side, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, this is Jon our SE.
[00:12] Lucas Chen: Hey all, Lucas here, quick note we just spun up a new GPU cluster, looking to partner on inference hosting.
[00:20] Jon Reyes: Nice, curious about your hardware mix and how you expose endpoints, do you do multi-tenant hosted API or per-customer dedicated VPCs?
[00:33] Amira Singh: Mostly multi-tenant today for smaller customers, but for enterprise we offer VPC peering and dedicated nodes.
[00:42] Tom Ruiz: We want to explore a deeper integration where Redwood could use VectorGrid for Dedicated capacity offering, potentially co-branded marketplace listing.
[00:51] Maya: Awesome  high level we support hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Private deployments in customer VPCs. Our key questions are latency SLAs, network path for model artifacts, and how we authenticate to your infra.
[01:08] Lucas: Latency target for our customers is typically sub-80ms for 2k token generation on optimized models, but we can tune. How do you handle KV cache and batching?
[01:20] Jon: We do continuous batching with intelligent policy based on token distribution, and we have prefix/KV cache that can be colocated with runtime. There might be some jargon swap  KV cache sometimes shows up as K-V chache in our notes.
[01:36] Amira Singh: We need to know if you require inbound ports open for KV sync or if you can work with a pull model from an S3-backed artifact store. Security is big  SOC 2, SSO via SAML, and customer key management via KMS/HSMs.
[01:55] Maya: Yeah that's expected. We support SAML SSO and can integrate with customer KMS; for Private we run a customer-controlled control plane and key material stays in your KMS. We'll share our security pack after this call.
[02:10] Tom: On billing, VectorGrid is used to revenue share on marketplace deployments. How flexible is Redwood's billing for partner rev-share or marketplace listing?
[02:22] Maya: We have a marketplace-friendly model and can do split revenue or reseller flows. Need to sync legal/compliance details.
[02:30] Lucas: Can you run on quantized models? We often push 4-bit quant to increase density but want to keep quality.
[02:38] Jon: Yes we support quantized runtimes, and the runtime will select kernels based on model arch and sequence lengths. There are always some edge cases  we'll run a small compatibility checklist.
[02:50] Amira: Network wise we use AWS in us-east-1 + private peering in eu-west-1 for some clients. For private deployments we'll want to avoid public internet egress for inference payloads.
[03:05] Jon: We can do VPC peering, private endpoints, and we have options for on-prem air-gapped deployments  though that needs a deeper SE conversation.
[03:18] Maya: Who are the stakeholders on your side for a pilot?
[03:22] Lucas: Myself + Amira on infra + Tom on partnerships for commercial. We'll probably bring in a couple of product folks later.
[03:30] Maya: Great, we typically run a 4-week pilot: week 0 onboarding and infra validation, week 1 perf benchmarks, week 2 integration work, week 3 ramp and go/no-go.
[03:44] Tom: Sounds reasonable. Can you give an example of the artifacts you'll need?
[03:48] Jon: We'll need a network topology, expected QPS and p95 latency targets, model sizes and tokenization patterns, and sample prompts. If you're doing on-prem we need disk image access or install script.
[04:05] Amira: I'll prepare the topology and expected throughput numbers.
[04:10] Lucas: A question on data retention  some customers need strict retention windows, can Redwood support configurable retention and audit logs?
[04:18] Maya: Yes, we have per-customer retention settings and audit logs; for Private deployments logs can be exported to a customer SIEM.
[04:26] Tom: Any regulatory concerns for EU customers? Data residency?
[04:29] Maya: We support regional deployments and can pin model variants to region; for strict residency we'll recommend Private deployment.
[04:36] Lucas: Competitors we've looked at include Lambda and Paperspace  we're trying to evaluate integration depth and operational overhead.
[04:45] Jon: From a technical lens, we can show kernel selection, batching tradeoffs, and quantization effects on throughput & latency in a short benchmark. We also have observed some models require special quantization pipelines.
[05:00] Amira: On the network security front, we prefer SAML + IP allowlists and mutual TLS for internal service-to-service.
[05:09] Jon: We support mTLS for internal connections, and we can wire up gov-cloud equivalents if needed.
[05:15] Maya: Next step we'll share our partner deck and security pack; Jon will run an initial compatibility checklist. Can we tentatively schedule the technical deep dive for the week of March 23?
[05:27] Lucas: Yes that works.
[05:30] Tom: Quick ask  can you summarize potential integration models (1) marketplace listing with hosted infra, (2) managed dedicated capacity via VectorGrid, (3) private deployment in customer VPC?
[05:42] Maya: Sure: (1) Marketplace: Redwood routes hosted API to VectorGrid nodes behind the scenes with usage reporting; simplest go-to-market. (2) Managed Dedicated: Reserved pools on VectorGrid per customer or per account with SLA; more control and better p95. (3) Private: Customer runs in their VPC, Redwood control plane optional, full isolation. Each has tradeoffs re: ops, revenue split, and security.
[06:10] Lucas: For our enterprise customers the managed dedicated and private are most interesting.
[06:15] Jon: We'll prepare a short doc detailing network ports, artifact flow, and expected kernel/quantization compatibilities.
[06:23] Amira: Also want to understand ops responsibilities  who handles OS updates on the GPU nodes, who handles model failures, and rollback procedures.
[06:33] Maya: For Managed Dedicated we usually operate the inference runtime but coordinate maintenance windows; for Private deployments the customer ops team owns the host layer and we support runtime updates via controlled rollouts.
[06:48] Tom: Anything else on compliance? We tend to ask customers for SOC2 attestation and evidence of key management.
[06:55] Maya: We'll include SOC2 certificate, pen test summary, and KMS integration docs in the security pack.
[07:02] Lucas: Last quick one  are there any hard limits on model size? We run some 70B models and a few custom weights.
[07:09] Jon: We support large models; limits are more a function of node memory and quantization. For 70B we typically recommend multi-GPU sharded runs or quantized runtimes.
[07:20] Amira: Great. We'll expect Jon's checklist and Maya's deck.
[07:24] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items discussed.
[07:28] Tom: Appreciate it.
[07:30] -- end of recorded transcript (auto transcription had minor mislabels and a few swapped words)
